final_text:
The data show a strong Enterobacteriaceae signal, but not enough to name the species.

- About 44,000 reads (8.9% of the report) are assigned directly to the family Enterobacteriaceae, with nothing resolved below it. That is the largest bacterial signal.
- Escherichia coli has only 154 reads, and Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Shigella and Citrobacter have a handful each. Salmonella has no reads at all.
- This pattern looks like a database or classification limit within the family, so the species stays unresolved.
- The technician's note says qPCR confirmed Salmonella enterica, but no instrument report is attached. The Kraken2 data do not support it, so I can't treat it as confirmed.

The most that can be said is that the sepsis is probably an Enterobacteriaceae infection, with the species undetermined. Species-level confirmation would need the attached qPCR report, blood culture, or a species-level re-analysis.
